component.name: once
component.title: Once
component.description: Send a single message to the route once, after the route starts, which is useful for development and testing.
component.label: core,scheduling

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

delay.label: advanced
delay.description: The default number of milliseconds that an endpoint of this component waits, after its route has started, before the consumer sends the message. The delay option of the endpoint replaces it. Use 0 or a negative value to send the message at once.

languages.label: advanced
languages.description: Whether a value of the body, headers, variables or exchangeProperties option that starts with language:NAME: is evaluated as an expression of the Camel language NAME, for example language:simple:${camelId}. If false, or if NAME is not a known language, the consumer uses the value as plain text, including the language:NAME: prefix.

consumerOut.description: No body without the body option. The body option gives its text, the text of a file:, classpath: or http: resource, a Boolean for true or false, a number for a whole number, or with language:NAME: the result of the expression

name.description: A name of your choice for the endpoint. The consumer also uses it in the name of the thread that sends the message.

body.description: The body of the message. The text true or false (in any case) becomes a Boolean, and a whole number becomes an Integer, or a Long if it is too large for an Integer. A value with a resource prefix such as file:, classpath: or http: is replaced by the text of that resource, and a value that starts with language:NAME: is evaluated as an expression, as described for the languages option of the component. The consumer sets the body last, so an expression can use the headers, exchange properties and variables. If not set, the body is null.

headers.description: The headers of the message, as key=value pairs, for example header.foo=abc. Each value is converted, loaded from a resource or evaluated as an expression in the same way as the body option. A value that results in null sets no header. This is a multi-value option with prefix: header.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

delay.label: advanced
delay.description: The number of milliseconds that the consumer waits, after the route has started, before it sends the message. Use 0 or a negative value to send the message at once. If not set, the delay option of the component applies.

exchangeProperties.label: advanced
exchangeProperties.description: The exchange properties, as key=value pairs, for example exchangeProperty.foo=abc. Each value is converted, loaded from a resource or evaluated as an expression in the same way as the body option. The consumer sets them after the variables and before the headers and the body. This is a multi-value option with prefix: exchangeProperty.

variables.label: advanced
variables.description: The exchange variables, as key=value pairs, for example variable.foo=abc. Each value is converted, loaded from a resource or evaluated as an expression in the same way as the body option. The consumer sets the variables first, so an expression in the other options can use them. This is a multi-value option with prefix: variable.
